title: Actuator works, but its feedback never arrives
summary: A contactor pulls in or a valve moves, yet the confirmation input stays unchanged, and every step that waits for it stalls.

sections.heading: Why feedback matters
sections.body: Programs rarely trust a command alone. A contactor's auxiliary contact, a valve's limit switch or a drive's running relay confirms that the actuator really did what it was told. The next step of a sequence, a lamp or an alarm is built on that confirmation.

sections.heading: Recognizing it
sections.body: The output is ON, the terminal carries 24 V and the device visibly responds, but the feedback input does not change. Everything that depends on the confirmation stays off, and a well-designed program raises a feedback timeout alarm.

sections.heading: Typical causes
sections.body: An auxiliary contact block not fitted or not wired, a broken or loose feedback wire, a limit switch that is misadjusted, or a feedback wired to another input than the drawing shows.

troubleshooting.effect: Steps that wait for the confirmation never continue
symptoms: The actuator works, but the machine never reports it
Lamps or follow-up steps that depend on the confirmation stay off
evidence: Output ON and device responding while the feedback input stays unchanged
The program waits for the feedback signal
diagnosticMethod: Energize the actuator and watch its feedback input
Measure the feedback contact and follow its wire to the input terminal
repair: Restore the feedback contact and its wiring, then repeat the test
troubleshooting.explanation: A confirmation that never arrives stops everything built on it, although the actuator itself works. Test every feedback during commissioning, not only the command.
